sentences.text: WOMAN: Hello, Oyster Bay Sailing Club.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 你好，牡蛎湾帆船俱乐部。

sentences.text: How can I help you?
sentences.zh: 我能帮您什么忙吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Oh hi.
sentences.zh: MAN: 哦，你好。

sentences.text: I'd like to find out about sailing courses for beginners.
sentences.zh: 我想了解一下针对初学者的帆船课程。

sentences.text: WOMAN: No problem.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 没问题。

sentences.text: Is it for yourself?
sentences.zh: 这是为您本人报名的吗？

sentences.text: MAN: Yes.
sentences.zh: MAN: 是的。

sentences.text: I had a look online but I'm not sure which course would be best.
sentences.zh: 我之前在网上查过，但不太确定哪门课程最适合我。

sentences.text: WOMAN: OK.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 好的。

sentences.text: Well you might be interested in our Taster Days?
sentences.zh: 嗯，您可能对我们的‘体验日’课程感兴趣？

sentences.text: MAN: Possibly.
sentences.zh: MAN: 有可能。

sentences.text: WOMAN: So these are for people who've never sailed before – it's basically an introduction to sailing to find out whether you enjoy it and want to carry on with it.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 这些课程面向从未接触过帆船的人——本质上是帆船入门介绍，旨在帮助您了解自己是否喜欢这项运动，并决定是否继续深入学习。

sentences.text: MAN: And how much is that?
sentences.zh: MAN: 那费用是多少？

sentences.text: WOMAN: It's £120 for the day - but it's reduced to £110 each if there are two of you.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 一天课程收费120英镑——但如果两人一同报名，则每人只需110英镑。

sentences.text: MAN: No, it would just be me.
sentences.zh: MAN: 不，就我一个人。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Oh that's fine.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 哦，没问题。

sentences.text: You'd be in a small group, usually about eight people but no more than ten – and everyone's always very friendly.
sentences.zh: 您将加入一个小班，通常约八人，最多不超过十人——而且大家总是非常友好。

sentences.text: MAN: Uh huh.
sentences.zh: MAN: 嗯。

sentences.text: And are there any other suitable courses?
sentences.zh: 还有其他合适的课程吗？

sentences.text: WOMAN: The other option is the Level 1 course.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 另一个选择是1级课程。

sentences.text: These are two-day weekend courses and we run those all year round.
sentences.zh: 这些是为期两天的周末课程，我们全年都开设。

sentences.text: MAN: OK.
sentences.zh: MAN: 好的。

sentences.text: And what do you learn on that course?
sentences.zh: 那么，你在该课程中会学到什么？

sentences.text: WOMAN: This is a mix of theory and practical skills.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 这门课程理论与实践技能相结合。

sentences.text: So you learn about things like the weather, which is obviously really important and also the tides, as well as learning basic sailing skills.
sentences.zh: 因此，你将学习诸如天气（这显然非常重要）以及潮汐等知识，同时还会掌握基础的帆船驾驶技能。

sentences.text: You go out into the harbour in special training dinghies for beginners, two people in each dinghy and an instructor.
sentences.zh: 你们将乘坐专为初学者设计的训练小艇出海进入港口，每艘小艇两人，并配备一名教练。

sentences.text: He or she will make sure you understand everything you need to know about safety.
sentences.zh: 这位教练会确保你充分理解所有必要的安全知识。

sentences.text: MAN: It sounds like hard work!
sentences.zh: MAN: 听起来挺辛苦的！

sentences.text: WOMAN: Yes, but you'll have a lot of fun too.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 是的，但你也会玩得很开心。

sentences.text: MAN: And the cost of that one is... ?
sentences.zh: MAN: 那这门课程的费用是……？

sentences.text: WOMAN: £200.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 200英镑。

sentences.text: But it's a bit cheaper if you decide to join the club.
sentences.zh: 不过，如果你决定加入俱乐部，费用会略低一些。

sentences.text: There's a discount for members.
sentences.zh: 会员可享受折扣。

sentences.text: MAN: Well, I'm not sure about that yet.
sentences.zh: MAN: 嗯，我目前还不确定是否要加入。

sentences.text: WOMAN: You've got plenty of time to decide.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 你还有充足的时间来决定。

sentences.text: MAN: And does the cost include everything?
sentences.zh: MAN: 那费用是否包含所有项目？

sentences.text: WOMAN: Yes, everything's included and you also get a really good dictionary explaining all the sailing terminology.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 是的，所有费用均已包含在内；此外，你还将获得一本非常实用的词典，其中详细解释了所有帆船术语。

sentences.text: A lot of people struggle with this at first.
sentences.zh: 很多人刚开始时对这些术语感到困难。

sentences.text: It's got lots of pictures, so I'm sure you'd find it really helpful.
sentences.zh: 这本词典配有大量插图，我相信你会觉得它非常有帮助。

sentences.text: And on completion of the course you get a certificate.
sentences.zh: 课程结束后，你将获得结业证书。

sentences.text: Then you're ready to move on to the Level 2 course.
sentences.zh: 然后你就可以进入二级课程了。

sentences.text: MAN: Sounds good.
sentences.zh: MAN: 听起来不错。

sentences.text: WOMAN: I think that's all the info you need for now.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 我觉得目前你需要的信息就这些了。

sentences.text: Just a couple of general things.
sentences.zh: 再简单提几点注意事项。

sentences.text: For example, it's really important that you know how to swim.
sentences.zh: 例如，你必须掌握游泳技能，这一点非常重要。

sentences.text: MAN: Yes, I'm pretty confident in the water.
sentences.zh: MAN: 是的，我在水里相当自信。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Great.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 太好了。

sentences.text: The other thing I should tell you is that we provide wetsuits and life jackets but you need to bring swimming trunks and some old trainers.
sentences.zh: 另外我要提醒你的是，我们会提供潜水服和救生衣，但你需要自备泳裤和一双旧运动鞋。

sentences.text: MAN: And a towel?
sentences.zh: MAN: 那毛巾呢？

sentences.text: WOMAN: Yes definitely.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 对，一定要带。

sentences.text: And you might want to bring your own toiletries, things like shampoo.
sentences.zh: 你可能还想自带洗漱用品，比如洗发水之类的。

sentences.text: MAN: OK.
sentences.zh: MAN: 好的。

sentences.text: What about food and drink?
sentences.zh: 那食物和饮料呢？

sentences.text: Do I need to bring that or is there a café at the club?
sentences.zh: 我需要自己带，还是俱乐部里有咖啡馆？

sentences.text: WOMAN: Yes, you can get sandwiches, cakes and snacks there.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 有的，那里可以买到三明治、蛋糕和零食。

sentences.text: The food's pretty reasonable.
sentences.zh: 食物价格相当合理。

sentences.text: MAN: OK good.
sentences.zh: MAN: 好的，不错。

sentences.text: Well I think I'm interested in the Level 1 course.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我对一级课程很感兴趣。

sentences.text: But I know absolutely nothing about sailing so is there anything I can do to prepare myself a bit?
sentences.zh: 但我对帆船运动一无所知，那么有没有什么我可以提前做的准备呢？

sentences.text: WOMAN: I recommend you watch some videos we use for training.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 我建议你观看我们培训时使用的一些视频。

sentences.text: They're available online.
sentences.zh: 它们可以在网上获取。

sentences.text: I can send you the link.
sentences.zh: 我可以把链接发给你。

sentences.text: They'll give you an idea of what to expect.
sentences.zh: 它们会帮你了解自己可以期待什么。

sentences.text: MAN: Perfect, thanks.
sentences.zh: 男士：太好了，谢谢。

sentences.text: That would be very helpful.
sentences.zh: 那将非常有帮助。

sentences.text: Oh and just one other thing - I'll be cycling to the club and will need somewhere to put valuables.
sentences.zh: 哦，还有一件事——我将骑自行车去俱乐部，需要一个地方存放贵重物品。

sentences.text: I'm just wondering if there are lockers for people to use?
sentences.zh: 我想知道是否有供人们使用的储物柜？

sentences.text: WOMAN: Yes, there are plenty in the changing rooms.
sentences.zh: 女士：是的，更衣室里有很多。

sentences.text: MAN: Great.
sentences.zh: 男士：太好了。

sentences.text: OK well could you book me onto...
sentences.zh: 好的，那么你能帮我报名参加……

sentences.text: MAN: Hello and welcome to the film making podcast.
sentences.zh: MAN: 你好，欢迎收听本期电影制作播客。

sentences.text: In this week's episode, Claire Lemarre talks to us about how to become a makeup artist.
sentences.zh: 本周节目中，克莱尔·勒马尔将与我们分享如何成为一名化妆师。

sentences.text: Claire's been working as a makeup artist in the film industry for over 20 years and has lots of useful advice about how to get started.
sentences.zh: 克莱尔已在电影行业担任化妆师超过20年，她就如何入行提供了大量实用建议。

sentences.text: WOMAN: Thanks Ian.
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 谢谢伊恩。

sentences.text: Well, before you can become a makeup artist on films you have to spend about 2 years working as a makeup trainee.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在你成为电影化妆师之前，你需先以化妆助理身份工作约两年。

sentences.text: A good place to get your first job would be on a low budget short film.
sentences.zh: 获得第一份工作的理想途径是参与低成本短片的拍摄。

sentences.text: Of course, this means that you'll be working for free.
sentences.zh: 当然，这意味着你将无偿工作。

sentences.text: But it's often worth it for the experience.
sentences.zh: 但这种经历往往物有所值。

sentences.text: Make sure your transport costs are covered – and remember, there's very unlikely to be any catering provided, so bring plenty of food.
sentences.zh: 务必确保交通费用有人承担——另外请记住，剧组极不可能提供餐饮服务，因此请自备充足的食物。

sentences.text: If you're lucky, you might start out on a big budget film where you'll get the most useful experience.
sentences.zh: 如果你运气好，或许能从高预算影片起步，从而获得最有价值的经验。

sentences.text: On productions like this, makeup and hair styling are separate departments – so you won't need to bring your curling tongs!
sentences.zh: 在这样的制作项目中，化妆与发型设计是两个独立部门——因此你无需自带卷发棒！

sentences.text: But you're likely to get the opportunity to work with a range of age groups, as well as different ethnicities.
sentences.zh: 但你很可能会有机会为不同年龄段及不同族裔的人士化妆。

sentences.text: Doing makeup for special effects is highly specialised, so don't expect to be offered any practical experience in that.
sentences.zh: 特效化妆高度专业化，因此不要指望能获得这方面的实操经验。

sentences.text: One problem with working in the makeup department is that it's a high-pressure environment.
sentences.zh: 在化妆部门工作的一个问题是，这是一份高压工作。

sentences.text: There are very few times when you'll be bored or have nothing to do.
sentences.zh: 你极少会感到无聊或无事可做。

sentences.text: It can be stressful but you'll see that the top makeup artists are very professional – even when they're having to work with directors who are impatient, or unhappy with the makeup artist's work.
sentences.zh: 这可能令人紧张，但你会发现顶尖化妆师都非常专业——即便面对缺乏耐心或对化妆效果不满的导演时也是如此。

sentences.text: Follow your supervisor's lead and try to remain calm at all times.
sentences.zh: 请以你的主管为榜样，并始终努力保持冷静。

sentences.text: I've worked with many very famous actors over the years.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我曾与许多著名演员合作过。

sentences.text: At first, I found it overwhelming and could hardly speak, I was so in awe.
sentences.zh: 起初，我感到不知所措，因敬畏而几乎说不出话来。

sentences.text: That's preferable, by the way, to becoming too excited and asking for selfies.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这总比过度兴奋、向他们索要自拍合影要好得多。

sentences.text: Now meeting the talent is just a normal part of the job and to be honest most actors don't look that special without all the makeup!
sentences.zh: 现在与演员见面只是工作中的常规部分，说实话，大多数演员卸了妆后看起来并没有那么特别！

sentences.text: Every makeup trainee will need a makeup kit, which they'll be expected to have with them at all times.
sentences.zh: 每位化妆学徒都需要配备一套化妆工具包，并且需要随时随身携带。

sentences.text: Just the essentials will do for the kinds of tasks you'll be given – it won't be anything complicated.
sentences.zh: 对于你们将要承担的任务而言，只需准备一些基本用品即可——不会有任何复杂的要求。

sentences.text: It's worth looking at what the other makeup artists have in their kits – but whatever you do, don't borrow anything without asking first.
sentences.zh: 值得参考其他化妆师的工具包里都装了些什么——但无论如何，请务必先征得同意再借用任何物品。

sentences.text: It's very important to build your portfolio.
sentences.zh: 建立个人作品集非常重要。

sentences.text: You should take photos of all the work you do and ideally show the different stages of makeup application if you can.
sentences.zh: 你应该为自己完成的所有工作拍照，理想情况下，最好能展示化妆过程的不同阶段。

sentences.text: But remember you'll need to get approval from the makeup designer in charge of the department.
sentences.zh: 但请记住，你必须事先获得负责该部门的化妆设计师的批准。

sentences.text: As you'll be sending your portfolio digitally, you won't need to get photos printed.
sentences.zh: 由于你的作品集将以数字形式发送，因此无需冲洗照片。

sentences.text: WOMAN: So what does a makeup trainee actually do?
sentences.zh: WOMAN: 那么，化妆学徒实际上要做些什么呢？

sentences.text: You need to think about whether you're the right kind of person to do the job and whether you'd enjoy it.
sentences.zh: 你需要思考自己是否适合这份工作，以及是否真的会享受这份工作。

sentences.text: So, to give you some idea, here are some of the things you might be required to do.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了让你有个大致了解，以下是一些你可能被要求完成的任务。

sentences.text: You may be asked to help prep an actor ready for makeup.
sentences.zh: 你可能会被要求协助演员做好上妆前的准备工作。

sentences.text: Some actors will arrive having already cleansed and moisturized their skin.
sentences.zh: 有些演员到场时已经完成了洁面和保湿护肤。

sentences.text: But sometimes you'll need to step in and get this done without wasting any time, otherwise the makeup artist will get behind schedule.
sentences.zh: 但有时你需要迅速介入并完成这些步骤，否则化妆师的工作进度就会延误。

sentences.text: Trainees play a useful role in continuity.
sentences.zh: 学徒在妆容连贯性方面发挥着重要作用。

sentences.text: It will be your responsibility to take photos, log them digitally and print out a hard copy to put in each actor's file.
sentences.zh: 你需要负责拍照、将照片以数字方式归档，并打印一份纸质版放入每位演员的档案中。

sentences.text: This information needs to be kept in good order as a reshoot can mean replicating makeup months later.
sentences.zh: 这些信息必须妥善保存，因为补拍可能意味着数月后重新复制同样的妆容。

sentences.text: General duties mean doing anything from getting the teas and coffees to putting on a wash.
sentences.zh: 日常杂务包括从沏茶倒咖啡到洗衣服等各种事情。

sentences.text: Having a positive attitude and being willing to do whatever is asked of you will help you get your next film job.
sentences.zh: 保持积极的态度，并乐于接受任何交办的任务，将有助于你获得下一部电影的工作机会。

sentences.text: You won't be asked to apply makeup to any of the principal cast, only the extras.
sentences.zh: 你不会被要求为任何主要演员化妆，仅需为群演化妆。

sentences.text: If there are dozens of extras involved you'll need to keep up a swift pace and not spend too long on each person.
sentences.zh: 如果涉及到几十个临时演员，你就需要保持快速的节奏，不能在每个人身上花费太多时间。

sentences.text: It takes quite a lot of confidence to be able to do this well.
sentences.zh: 要很好地做到这一点，需要相当大的信心。

sentences.text: OK now about terms and conditions....
sentences.zh: 好的，现在来谈谈条款和条件……

sentences.text: PHIL: That lecture from the visiting speaker yesterday was good, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: PHIL: 昨天那位来访演讲者的讲座很不错，对吧？

sentences.text: LUCY: Yeah.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是啊。

sentences.text: I learned a lot from her about ocean biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 我从她那里学到了很多关于海洋生物多样性的知识。

sentences.text: I've already done some reading on it, and I did an assignment on some of the problems associated with it last year, but I especially liked the way her lecture focused on more long-term issues.
sentences.zh: 我之前已经就此做过一些阅读，而且去年还完成过一份关于相关问题的作业，但我尤其喜欢她讲座中聚焦于更长期议题的方式。

sentences.text: PHIL: Yes, things that aren't currently receiving widespread attention but are likely to be important in the future.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 没错，就是那些目前尚未受到广泛关注、但未来很可能变得十分重要的问题。

sentences.text: That impressed me too.
sentences.zh: 这一点也给我留下了深刻印象。

sentences.text: It wasn't exactly a feel-good conclusion because it's hard to see any real solution for a lot of the problems.
sentences.zh: 不过，那并非一个令人安心的结论，因为许多问题似乎根本看不到切实可行的解决方案。

sentences.text: LUCY: No, though she did point to where policy changes could be made to protect our marine and coastal environments.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是的，尽管她确实指出了可在哪些方面调整政策，以保护我们的海洋与沿海环境。

sentences.text: PHIL: Mm.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 嗯。

sentences.text: But that's just at a national level.
sentences.zh: 但那仅限于国家层面。

sentences.text: The examples she gave were at a more global level, and they really made it clear to me just how wide-ranging the threats to ocean biodiversity are.
sentences.zh: 她所举的例子则处于更广泛的全球层面，这让我真切意识到海洋生物多样性所面临的威胁范围之广。

sentences.text: LUCY: Yes, me too.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是的，我也有同感。

sentences.text: PHIL: The research project she described was impressive, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: PHIL: 她所描述的这项研究项目令人印象深刻，不是吗？

sentences.text: I'd have thought it was quite unusual to have so many experts working together.
sentences.zh: 我原以为，能有如此多专家共同协作，实属罕见。

sentences.text: LUCY: Yeah, and from such different backgrounds.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是啊，而且他们来自如此迥异的背景。

sentences.text: Must have been a really exciting team to work with.
sentences.zh: 想必那支团队合作起来一定非常令人振奋。

sentences.text: I'd heard of a couple of them before – they were involved in research way back in 2009 warning about the dangers of ocean pollution.
sentences.zh: 我之前就听说过其中几位——早在2009年，他们就参与了有关海洋污染危害的预警研究。

sentences.text: PHIL: But now people are much more aware of that, aren't they?
sentences.zh: PHIL: 但如今人们对这个问题的关注度已高得多，不是吗？

sentences.text: LUCY: I suppose so.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 我想是这样。

sentences.text: PHIL: Another thing about the research is that the team members came from all round the world.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 这项研究的另一特点是，团队成员来自世界各地。

sentences.text: Though I suppose that's not unusual nowadays, now everyone can work remotely.
sentences.zh: 虽然我想，如今这已不足为奇，毕竟现在人人都可以远程办公。

sentences.text: LUCY: Right.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 好的。

sentences.text: I liked the way she didn't bombard us with figures – I mean, they were available, but she focused more on the general points they indicated.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢她没有用大量数据轰炸我们——我的意思是，那些数据确实可供查阅，但她更侧重于阐述这些数据所体现的总体要点。

sentences.text: PHIL: Mm.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 嗯。

sentences.text: And the description of improvements in systems used for tracking marine animals and things like robots were really interesting.
sentences.zh: 关于追踪海洋动物的系统改进以及机器人等技术的介绍，真的非常有趣。

sentences.text: LUCY: Yes, and her description of how robotics can be used to investigate threats to biodiversity.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是的，还有她对如何利用机器人技术调查生物多样性威胁的描述。

sentences.text: PHIL: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 没错。

sentences.text: PHIL: While you're here, can we talk about the list of resources we have to evaluate for the seminar tomorrow.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 既然你在这儿，我们能聊聊明天研讨会需要评估的资源清单吗？

sentences.text: I've had a look at them all, but it's been a bit of a rush.
sentences.zh: 我已通读了全部资料，但时间有点仓促。

sentences.text: LUCY: Yeah.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 是啊。

sentences.text: What did you think of that article on invasive lionfish?
sentences.zh: 你觉得那篇关于入侵性狮子鱼的文章怎么样？

sentences.text: The one claiming they were expanding their habitat throughout the Mediterranean Sea.
sentences.zh: 就是那篇声称它们正将栖息地扩展至整个地中海海域的文章。

sentences.text: PHIL: Well, the writer went on about how dangerous they were in environmental terms, which is probably true, but he didn't really provide much information to explain why.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 嗯，作者大谈特谈它们在环境方面的危害性，这或许属实，但他并未提供太多信息来解释原因。

sentences.text: LUCY: I know what you mean.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 我明白你的意思。

sentences.text: PHIL: I watched the documentary on microplastics, at least I started to, but then I found it was made ten years ago so I gave up.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 我看了关于微塑料的纪录片，至少一开始看了，但后来发现它竟是十年前制作的，于是就放弃了。

sentences.text: LUCY: I watched to the end but you're right, it was showing its age.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 我看完了，不过你说得对，片子确实显得过时了。

sentences.text: People had hardly heard of microplastics then, whereas now everyone knows about them and how dangerous they are.
sentences.zh: 当时人们几乎还没听说过微塑料，而如今人人都知道它们及其危害性。

sentences.text: PHIL: Yeah.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 是啊。

sentences.text: Did you listen to the podcast on ocean pollution?
sentences.zh: 你听了那期关于海洋污染的播客了吗？

sentences.text: LUCY: Mm.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 嗯。

sentences.text: I didn't get anything out of it though.
sentences.zh: 不过，我从中什么也没学到。

sentences.text: Most of it was stating the obvious.
sentences.zh: 大部分内容都是在陈述显而易见的事实。

sentences.text: PHIL: Yes, it mentioned pesticides and plastic and things, and it clearly made the point that they were a bad thing, but everybody knows that anyway.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 是的，它提到了杀虫剂和塑料之类的东西，并明确指出它们是有害的，但这一点大家本来就知道。

sentences.text: Did you read that book on coastal ecosystems?
sentences.zh: 你读过那本关于海岸生态系统的书吗？

sentences.text: LUCY: The one by John Harper?
sentences.zh: LUCY: 就是约翰·哈珀写的那本？

sentences.text: Yes, I found it hard going at first, it went into a lot of detail about things like the effects of offshore windfarms and fish farms, but actually I ended up with a much better understanding of the issues.
sentences.zh: 是的，一开始我觉得读起来很吃力，书中详细探讨了近海风电场和水产养殖场的影响等问题，但最终我对相关议题的理解确实大大加深了。

sentences.text: PHIL: Yes, I agree and I thought it was a well-written summary of those.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 是的，我同意，而且我认为这本书对这些议题的总结写得相当好。

sentences.text: And the diagrams helped a lot too.
sentences.zh: 而且图示也帮了大忙。

sentences.text: LUCY: The article on metal toxicity was way above my head, I didn't know anything about how metals from industrial emissions react in the ocean... and I still don't understand it.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 关于金属毒性的那篇文章完全超出了我的理解范围，我对工业排放的金属在海洋中如何发生反应一无所知……现在还是不懂。

sentences.text: PHIL: I gave up reading after the first chapter – I just couldn't follow it.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 我读完第一章就放弃了——根本跟不上内容。

sentences.text: LUCY: That podcast on floating marine cities was interesting, though it presented a rather one-sided picture, I thought.
sentences.zh: LUCY: 不过，那个关于漂浮海上城市的播客倒挺有意思，尽管我觉得它呈现的画面有些片面。

sentences.text: PHIL: Yes, it focused on how this would benefit people and ignored the effects on the environment.
sentences.zh: PHIL: 是的，它只聚焦于这种城市将如何造福人类，却忽略了其对环境造成的影响。

sentences.text: LUCY: But anyway, shall we ...
sentences.zh: LUCY: 但不管怎样，我们是不是该……

sentences.text: Much of the world now lives in an industrial civilisation.
sentences.zh: 如今，世界上大部分地区都生活在工业文明之中。

sentences.text: But this has only become possible because we have the necessary natural resources.
sentences.zh: 但这种文明之所以成为可能，仅仅是因为我们拥有必要的自然资源。

sentences.text: There are three types of natural resource without which industry could not exist.
sentences.zh: 有三种自然资源是工业赖以生存的必要条件。

sentences.text: One of these is metal – without that we'd have no machines and no transportation.
sentences.zh: 其中一种是金属——没有金属，我们就无法制造机器和交通工具。

sentences.text: Another is fossil fuels, which we need to power those machines.
sentences.zh: 另一种是化石燃料，我们需要它来为这些机器提供动力。

sentences.text: But there's a third resource that's essential to connect the different parts of a machine together with belts and pipes and shock absorbers, and that is rubber.
sentences.zh: 但还有第三种资源同样至关重要，它用于通过皮带、管道和减震器将机器的不同部件连接起来，这种资源就是橡胶。

sentences.text: It's now used in over 40,000 products, from waterproof footwear to surgical gloves.
sentences.zh: 如今，橡胶已被应用于四万多种产品中，从防水鞋靴到外科手术手套不等。

sentences.text: At present, we have two types of rubber in common use.
sentences.zh: 目前，我们普遍使用的橡胶有两种。

sentences.text: One is natural rubber, which nearly all comes from the Pará rubber tree.
sentences.zh: 一种是天然橡胶，几乎全部来自巴西橡胶树（Pará rubber tree）。

sentences.text: This was originally native to Brazil, but is now cultivated on plantations in South-East Asia.
sentences.zh: 这种树原产于巴西，如今则主要在东南亚的种植园中栽培。

sentences.text: Recently, however, concern's been growing that supplies may soon be insufficient for the world's needs.
sentences.zh: 然而，近来人们日益担忧，天然橡胶的供应可能很快无法满足全球需求。

sentences.text: So what exactly is limiting the supply of natural rubber?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟是什么因素限制了天然橡胶的供应呢？

sentences.text: Well, for one thing, rubber trees don't just spring up overnight.
sentences.zh: 首先，橡胶树并不会一夜之间长成。

sentences.text: It can take eight to ten years for a tree to start producing rubber, so cultivating them's a slow process.
sentences.zh: 一棵树需要八到十年时间才能开始产胶，因此种植橡胶树是一个缓慢的过程。

sentences.text: And this leads to another problem.
sentences.zh: 而这又引发了另一个问题。

sentences.text: With most crops, farmers don't have to think very far ahead, so they can easily change what crop they produce, or how much of a crop they produce, if they find the demand for that crop is rising or falling.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数农作物而言，农民无需考虑太长远，因此一旦发现某种作物的需求上升或下降，他们可以轻松调整所种植的作物种类或产量。

sentences.text: But if you have to plant eight or ten years ahead, that's much harder.
sentences.zh: 但如果你必须提前八到十年规划种植，那就困难得多。

sentences.text: And also the rubber tree's very choosy about where it grows.
sentences.zh: 此外，橡胶树对生长环境极为挑剔。

sentences.text: It needs the right temperature, the right amount of rainfall, and the right altitude – not too high and not too low.
sentences.zh: 它需要适宜的温度、适量的降雨以及合适的海拔高度——既不能太高，也不能太低。

sentences.text: The result is that it can't be grown in the northern or southern parts of the globe, only around the equator.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，橡胶树无法在地球的北半球或南半球地区种植，只能生长在赤道附近。

sentences.text: Another problem is that the rubber is basically extracted in the same way as it's been done for hundreds of years, and that's by hand, by making small cuts in the trunk of the tree, and putting a little cup there to catch the latex, as the rubber is called.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，橡胶的提取方式基本上与数百年前相同，即通过人工在树干上切出小口，并放置一个小杯子来收集乳胶（也就是橡胶）。

sentences.text: It's very labour-intensive.
sentences.zh: 这非常耗费人力。

sentences.text: And it's not just the initial production that's limiting supplies.
sentences.zh: 而且，限制供应的不仅仅是最初的生产环节。

sentences.text: With other resources such as water and glass, when we've finished using them we can recycle them, but although this is also possible with rubber, it's very difficult, so that also reduces the amount we have available.
sentences.zh: 对于水和玻璃等其他资源，我们在使用完后可以回收利用，虽然橡胶也可以回收，但难度很大，因此这也减少了我们的可用量。

sentences.text: And in the last few years, there have been new threats to the supply of natural rubber.
sentences.zh: 而在过去几年中，天然橡胶的供应又面临新的威胁。

sentences.text: One problem is linked to the fact that nearly all the rubber trees in South-East Asia are descended from just a small number of seeds brought from Brazil in the nineteenth century.
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题是，东南亚几乎所有的橡胶树都源自19世纪从巴西引进的少量种子。

sentences.text: This means that there's very little genetic diversity among the trees, which in turn makes them very vulnerable to disease.
sentences.zh: 这意味着这些树木的遗传多样性极低，从而使它们极易受到疾病的侵袭。

sentences.text: The most dangerous threat is a fungus, which destroyed large numbers of rubber trees in Brazil, and which could cause devastation to plantations worldwide.
sentences.zh: 最危险的威胁是一种真菌，它曾摧毁了巴西大量橡胶树，也可能给全球橡胶种植园造成毁灭性打击。

sentences.text: Another problem is that farmers in South-East Asia are increasingly turning to the cultivation of palm oil, which is easier and more profitable for them.
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是，东南亚的农民正越来越多地转向种植棕榈油，因为这对他们而言更容易且利润更高。

sentences.text: And finally, in recent years South-East Asia, like other parts of the world, has been repeatedly hit by extreme types of weather, and this looks likely to continue in the future.
sentences.zh: 最后，近年来，东南亚地区像世界其他地区一样，屡遭极端天气袭击，而这种情况在未来似乎仍将持续。

sentences.text: However, as well as using natural rubber, it's also possible to make rubber synthetically.
sentences.zh: 然而，除了使用天然橡胶外，我们还可以人工合成橡胶。

sentences.text: This works very well for some purposes, for example, making engine parts, or silicone pots and pans used for cooking.
sentences.zh: 这种合成橡胶在某些用途上效果很好，例如制造发动机零件，或用于烹饪的硅胶锅具。

sentences.text: But compared with natural rubber, it's not anything like as strong, and this means it can't replace natural rubber in other products.
sentences.zh: 但与天然橡胶相比，它的强度远远不足，因此无法在其他产品中替代天然橡胶。

sentences.text: For example, while a mixture of natural rubber and synthetic rubber works well in car tyres, only natural rubber can stand up to the extreme speeds of aircraft tyres during take-off and landing.
sentences.zh: 例如，汽车轮胎中天然橡胶与合成橡胶的混合物效果良好，但只有天然橡胶才能承受飞机轮胎在起飞和降落时的极端速度。

sentences.text: So for some time, scientists have been looking for alternative sources of natural rubber.
sentences.zh: 因此，长期以来，科学家一直在寻找天然橡胶的替代来源。

sentences.text: One that's been known about for some time seems initially to be a rather unlikely source.
sentences.zh: 其中一种早已为人所知的替代来源，初看似乎相当不太可能。

sentences.text: It's a wild plant with yellow flowers that we normally regard as a weed when we see it in our gardens.
sentences.zh: 这是一种开黄花的野生植物，我们通常在自家花园里见到它时，会把它当作杂草。

sentences.text: But when it's pulled up and its roots cut open, they're found to contain rubber.
sentences.zh: 但当它被连根拔起并切开根部时，人们发现其根部含有橡胶。

sentences.text: Now, compared to the rubber tree, dandelions produce relatively small amounts of rubber, but unlike rubber trees, they're very adaptable.
sentences.zh: 与橡胶树相比，蒲公英产生的橡胶量相对较少，但与橡胶树不同，蒲公英适应性极强。

sentences.text: They'll grow in all sorts of places, and they don't need rich soil.
sentences.zh: 它们能在各种地方生长，且不需要肥沃的土壤。

sentences.text: So at present there are several projects underway investigating the possibility of using dandelions as a source of rubber.
sentences.zh: 目前，有多个项目正在开展，研究将蒲公英作为橡胶来源的可能性。

sentences.text: Another possibility is a desert shrub grown in Mexico and Texas ...
sentences.zh: 另一种可能性是在墨西哥和得克萨斯州种植的一种沙漠灌木……
